 Petrol prices fall to lowest point since July; Diesel also getting cheaper 
 Thursday, 5 November 2026 - 12:50
 Petrol prices in the Netherlands dropped below 2.50 euros per liter on Thursday for the first time since early July. The decrease is driven by falling oil prices in recent weeks.
 UnitedConsumers puts the current recommended price of petrol at 2.485 euros per liter, a decrease of more than 2 cents compared to Wednesday. The price had hit a record high of 2.732 euros per liter on October 10.
 Diesel prices also dropped on Thursday to 2.647 euros per liter, 18 cents below the record of 2.824 euros set in mid-September. Premium petrol (Euro98) has seen an even sharper decline, falling 25 cents in less than a month to 2.698 euros per liter.
 UnitedConsumers calculates an average based on the recommended prices published daily by major oil companies. These rates are typically found at more expensive petrol stations, particularly those along highways, while other stations often offer lower prices.
 Although petrol prices have fallen in recent weeks, filling up in the Netherlands is still considerably more expensive than in neighbouring countries. High fuel taxes, which rank among the highest in Europe, are a major factor. As a result, many Dutch motorists have been travelling to Belgium to take advantage of lower fuel prices.
 Oil prices have declined as hopes grow for a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East. Before the conflict began in late February, the recommended price of Euro95 petrol was 2.285 euros per liter, while diesel cost 2.084 euros per liter.
 Reporting by ANP
